test_type: integration (AbstractIntegrationTest + Testcontainers Mongo) — correct: validation performs a real DB lookup, so mocking would be the wrong type
summary: Six SUBSCRIBE tests, each earning its place: required (null+blank), not_found (missing/malformed/foreign-project — three distinct code paths to one code), step_not_found, draft-allowed + full round-trip, activation-blocks-on-inactive (negative+positive), and (added in this review) activation-blocks-when-any-second-target-inactive to lock the per-step loop. Assertions check real results (codes, HTTP status, response DTO fields, DB-persisted step), not mock calls. Tests isolated via @BeforeEach deleteAll.

findings.title: Stated edge case 'multiple SUBSCRIBE steps, fail on first inactive' was not covered
findings.detail: Task lists multiple-SUBSCRIBE-steps as an edge case (validate each; activation fails on the first non-active). The single-step activation test did not exercise the loop over >1 SUBSCRIBE step.
findings.reason: Low-cost test locking a stated edge case (the requireSubscribeTargetsActive loop). Added subscribe_activate_blocksWhenAnySecondTargetInactive (first target active, second draft → still 422 inactive). Green.

findings.title: endParentAfter=false round-trip not separately asserted
findings.detail: Round-trip test asserts endParentAfter=true; the false default is exercised on save in other tests but not asserted on the persisted step.
findings.reason: Boolean primitive mapping is Task 1 territory; the true case already proves the wiring. Adding a false-assertion gives marginal confidence.
